newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PARLIAMENT PASSES SAVINGS COMPENSATION LAW.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT PASSES SAVINGS COMPENSATION LAW.

text.p: Parliament passed a law on Thursday to compensate people who lost savings to hyper-inflation and had accounts confiscated by Soviet banks in the chaos surrounding the breakup of the former Soviet Union.

Repaying the deposits is expected to cost around 3.2 billion litas. The law says that no less than two thirds of funds from the privatisation of state assets will be transferred to the deposit compensation fund to pay for the scheme.

Analysts and diplomats have questioned the move, saying it will be difficult to raise the compensation money through privatisation, as the government plans and that the money could be better used for investments.

"Seventy-five percent of the privatisation money will go to compensation, not for investments, not for the future and not for jobs," said Kestutis Glaveckas, deputy head of parliament's finance and budget committee, who was against the law.
"The best alternative is that this money would go to funding private pension funds," said Glaveckas, a member of the Centre Union. The law was passed in a 74 to 4 vote.
The chairman of the finance and budget committe, Elvyra Kunevichiene, has said the first payments will be made at the start of next year.
Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said last week that the compensation process might take three years depending on the success of the privatisation process.
The law says priority will be given first to invalids, families with invalid children and people 85 years and older.
